templates.pattern:
What is the profit percentage of a trader who uses two different fraudulent methods simultaneously?
Statement I: The trader gives 10% less quantity than labelled while selling.
Statement II: The trader buys at 10% more quantity than he pays for.
Which statement(s) is/are sufficient to answer the question?
options: Option A: Statement I alone is sufficient
Option B: Statement II alone is sufficient
Option C: Both statements together are sufficient
Option D: Either statement alone is sufficient
templates.explanation: Effective gain from buying fraud: gets 110 for price of 100. Selling fraud: charges for 100 but gives 90. Combined profit% = (110/90 - 1)×100 = (20/90)×100 ≈ 22.22%. Both frauds are needed to compute combined profit. Both statements are needed.

templates.pattern:
A dishonest dealer sells goods at cost price but makes a profit. What is his profit percentage?
Statement I: He uses a weight of 800g instead of 1000g.
Statement II: He claims to give a 10% discount but actually gives only 5%.
Which statement(s) is/are sufficient to answer the question?
options: Option A: Statement I alone is sufficient
Option B: Statement II alone is sufficient
Option C: Both statements together are sufficient
Option D: Either statement alone is sufficient
templates.explanation: Statement I: Profit from false weight = (1000-800)/800×100 = 25%. The question says he sells at cost price — so Statement I alone fully explains the profit. Statement II adds a discount deception but the question specifies selling at cost price — Statement I alone is sufficient.

templates.pattern:
A man buys goods and sells part immediately and part after a year. What is his overall profit%?
Statement I: He buys 100 units at ₹50 each. He sells 60 units immediately at 20% profit.
Statement II: He sells remaining 40 units after a year at 10% loss.
Which statement(s) is/are sufficient to answer the question?
options: Option A: Statement I alone is sufficient
Option B: Statement II alone is sufficient
Option C: Both statements together are sufficient
Option D: Either statement alone is sufficient
templates.explanation: Total CP = 5000. SP1 = 60×50×1.2 = 3600. SP2 = 40×50×0.9 = 1800. Total SP = 5400. Profit% = 8%. Statement I gives part of the transaction. Statement II gives the remaining. Both needed for overall profit.

templates.pattern:
A shopkeeper has two pricing strategies. Under which strategy does he earn more profit?
Statement I: Strategy A: mark up 40%, give 25% discount.
Statement II: Strategy B: mark up 60%, give 35% discount.
Which statement(s) is/are sufficient to answer the question?
options: Option A: Statement I alone is sufficient
Option B: Statement II alone is sufficient
Option C: Both statements together are sufficient
Option D: Either statement alone is sufficient
templates.explanation: Strategy A profit% = 1.4×0.75-1 = 0.05 = 5%. Strategy B profit% = 1.6×0.65-1 = 0.04 = 4%. Strategy A gives more. Statement I alone gives Strategy A profit. Statement II alone gives Strategy B profit. Both needed to compare.

templates.pattern:
A company launches a product with promotional pricing. What is the actual profit percentage?
Statement I: The product costs ₹200 to manufacture and is marked at ₹350.
Statement II: A buy-one-get-one-free promotion is offered on the marked price.
Which statement(s) is/are sufficient to answer the question?
options: Option A: Statement I alone is sufficient
Option B: Statement II alone is sufficient
Option C: Both statements together are sufficient
Option D: Either statement alone is sufficient
templates.explanation: BOGO: customer pays for 1, gets 2. Effective SP per unit = 350/2 = ₹175. CP = ₹200. Loss% = (25/200)×100 = 12.5%. Statement I gives CP and MP. Statement II gives promotion type. Both needed to find effective SP and profit%.

templates.pattern:
What is the effective profit when goods are sold on instalment with interest?
Statement I: Goods costing ₹12,000 are sold in 12 monthly instalments of ₹1,200 each.
Statement II: The seller also charges 2% processing fee on total instalment amount.
Which statement(s) is/are sufficient to answer the question?
options: Option A: Statement I alone is sufficient
Option B: Statement II alone is sufficient
Option C: Both statements together are sufficient
Option D: Either statement alone is sufficient
templates.explanation: Total instalment = 12×1200 = 14400. Processing fee = 2% of 14400 = 288. Total received = 14688. Profit = 14688-12000 = 2688. Profit% = 22.4%. Statement I gives instalment details. Statement II gives processing fee. Both needed for total profit.

templates.pattern:
What is the profit percentage if unsold stock is written off?
Statement I: A trader buys 500 units at ₹40 each and sells 450 units at ₹55 each.
Statement II: Remaining 50 units are written off as unsaleable.
Which statement(s) is/are sufficient to answer the question?
options: Option A: Statement I alone is sufficient
Option B: Statement II alone is sufficient
Option C: Both statements together are sufficient
Option D: Either statement alone is sufficient
templates.explanation: Total CP = 500×40 = 20000. SP = 450×55 = 24750. Written off = 50×40 = 2000 (total CP unchanged). Profit = 24750-20000 = 4750. Profit% = 23.75%. Statement I gives sales. Statement II confirms write-off. Both needed for complete picture.

templates.pattern:
A trader gives different discounts to wholesale and retail buyers. What is his average profit%?
Statement I: Wholesale buyers (60% of sales) get 30% discount on MP. MP is 60% above CP.
Statement II: Retail buyers (40% of sales) get 15% discount on MP.
Which statement(s) is/are sufficient to answer the question?
options: Option A: Statement I alone is sufficient
Option B: Statement II alone is sufficient
Option C: Both statements together are sufficient
Option D: Either statement alone is sufficient
templates.explanation: Wholesale profit% = 1.6×0.7-1 = 12%. Retail profit% = 1.6×0.85-1 = 36%. Average = 0.6×12 + 0.4×36 = 7.2+14.4 = 21.6%. Statement I gives wholesale info and markup. Statement II gives retail discount. Both needed for average profit%.

templates.pattern:
What is the profit made by a contractor on a project?
Statement I: The contract value is ₹5,00,000. Material cost is ₹2,00,000 and labour cost is ₹1,50,000.
Statement II: Overhead and administrative expenses are 15% of total direct costs.
Which statement(s) is/are sufficient to answer the question?
options: Option A: Statement I alone is sufficient
Option B: Statement II alone is sufficient
Option C: Both statements together are sufficient
Option D: Either statement alone is sufficient
templates.explanation: Direct cost = 200000+150000 = 350000. Overhead = 15% of 350000 = 52500. Total cost = 402500. Profit = 500000-402500 = ₹97500. Statement I gives contract value and direct costs. Statement II gives overhead rate. Both needed.

templates.pattern:
What is the profit percentage if a shopkeeper sells at different prices on different days?
Statement I: On weekdays he sells 60 units per day at ₹120 each for 5 days. CP is ₹90 per unit.
Statement II: On weekends he sells 100 units per day at ₹105 each for 2 days.
Which statement(s) is/are sufficient to answer the question?
options: Option A: Statement I alone is sufficient
Option B: Statement II alone is sufficient
Option C: Both statements together are sufficient
Option D: Either statement alone is sufficient
templates.explanation: Weekday SP = 60×5×120 = 36000. Weekend SP = 100×2×105 = 21000. Total SP = 57000. Total units = 500. Total CP = 500×90 = 45000. Profit% = (12000/45000)×100 ≈ 26.67%. Both statements needed for complete weekly picture.

templates.pattern:
What is the profit percentage of a business after paying salaries and rent?
Statement I: Revenue is ₹2,00,000. Cost of goods sold is ₹1,00,000. Salaries are ₹30,000.
Statement II: Rent is ₹20,000 and miscellaneous expenses are 5% of revenue.
Which statement(s) is/are sufficient to answer the question?
options: Option A: Statement I alone is sufficient
Option B: Statement II alone is sufficient
Option C: Both statements together are sufficient
Option D: Either statement alone is sufficient
templates.explanation: Total cost = 100000+30000+20000+10000 = 160000. Profit = 200000-160000 = 40000. Profit% on cost = (40000/160000)×100 = 25%. Statement I gives COGS and salaries. Statement II gives rent and miscellaneous. Both needed for total profit%.

templates.pattern:
A company sells a product at different prices in domestic and export markets. What is overall profit%?
Statement I: 70% of production sold domestically at 30% profit. Production cost is ₹500 per unit.
Statement II: 30% of production exported at 40% profit after paying 10% export duty on selling price.
Which statement(s) is/are sufficient to answer the question?
options: Option A: Statement I alone is sufficient
Option B: Statement II alone is sufficient
Option C: Both statements together are sufficient
Option D: Either statement alone is sufficient
templates.explanation: Domestic SP = 500×1.3 = 650, profit = 150 per unit. Export SP = 500×1.4 = 700, duty = 70, net SP = 630, profit = 130 per unit. Overall profit per unit = 0.7×150 + 0.3×130 = 105+39 = 144. Overall profit% = (144/500)×100 = 28.8%. Both statements needed.

incorrect: Check if one or both statements are needed 🤔
